images.title: Same counters, either order
images.purpose: Show that swapping two terms keeps the same counters, so the value stays 2.
images.composition: Two horizontal rows of round counters, one under the other, with the sums at the left and the result at the right.
exact_structure: Top row: 6 green #009E73 circles each marked + followed by 4 vermilion #D55E00 circles each marked −, ten circles in one line.
Bottom row: 4 vermilion circles marked − followed by 6 green circles marked +, ten circles in one line.
Left of the top row the label 6 + (−4); left of the bottom row the label (−4) + 6.
At the right end of each row, = 2.
rejection: not 6 green and 4 vermilion in each row
the order of colours the same in both rows
images.takeaway: Swapping the two terms moves the same counters, so the value does not change.
images.description: Two rows of the same ten counters in opposite order, both worth 2.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text on swapping terms.
images.teaching_notes: Count the counters in each row and notice that only the order differs.

image_decisions.why: Counters make it plain that order does not change a sum of terms.
